title: Add traffic-partitioned spectator fingerprint rollout guard
author: Marcus Patel
description: Context: We observed intermittent rollouts where global canary signals were noisy because regressions only affected a small traffic partition (e.g., specific region, client shard, or long-tail prompt shapes). Motivation: introduce a lightweight 'spectator' fingerprinting detector that samples stratified traffic partitions and computes a distributional fingerprint (multi-metric: p50/p95 latency, per-route throughput, error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization) to detect correlated regressions that are masked in aggregate baselines. Design summary: 1) Spectator sampler runs as a low-overhead sidecar that mirrors ~0.5-2% of requests across configured partitions without affecting production routing. 2) For each partition we compute a compact histogram fingerprint and transform with PCA+KL divergence to a baseline window to detect distributional drift. 3) The rollout guard uses a hierarchical decision tree: partition-level drift -> correlated infra signal -> automatic slow-down and canary pause; otherwise annotate telemetry and continue. 4) The guard integrates with existing canary controller to emit reasons and suggested remediation (rollback, scale, route-shift). Checklist: - [x] core detector implementation and unit tests - [x] e2e simulation harness and synthetic regressions - [x] alerting rules and console dashboard panels - [x] canary controller hooks and annotation schema - [x] privacy review for mirrored sampling - [x] docs and runbook - [x] staged rollout in perf lab Testing: ran synthetic regressions (latency spike, per-route QPS skew, GPU contention) and validated guard actions in the perf-canary lab. Performance: spectator sidecar uses sampling and sketching to keep overhead <0.8% CPU and <1% added p95 on probe paths. Rollout plan: merge to main, deploy to perf-canary staging for 48h with sampling at 2%, then staged ramp to 0.5% in production for 7d. Related: builds on prior drift detectors but focuses on partitioned, distributional regressions; references ENG-6543. Risk and mitigation: false positives for ephemeral spikes mitigated via bootstrap baselines and persistence window, ability to mute partitions, and manual override in console.

review_comments: Avery Chen: Nice approach. Concern: PCA + KL pipeline might be sensitive to low QPS partitions. Can you add adaptive smoothing and a minimum sample threshold?
Marcus Patel: Added adaptive smoothing with exponential windowing and a configurable min_samples threshold; updated tests to cover <10 QPS behavior.
Sofia Lopez: We need clearer observability for why a guard paused a rollout. Please ensure reasons include the partition id, metric fingerprint delta, and correlated infra signal IDs.
Marcus Patel: Added annotation payload to canary controller and dashboard panels showing partition id, delta score, and infra signals (GPU util, OOM events).
Ethan Brooks: CI flake: test_histogram_sketch occasionally times out on small CI runners. Recommend increasing timeouts or adding a lightweight mock path.
Marcus Patel: Split heavy sketch tests into a slow/fast matrix and added a mock for CI. Re-ran CI.
Avery Chen: Approved after test matrix change and docs update. Left small nits in runbook.

release_notes: Add traffic-partitioned spectator fingerprint rollout guard: detects distributional regressions localized to traffic partitions and pauses rollouts when correlated infra signals are observed. Includes new detector, canary controller hooks, dashboards, alerts, and runbook.
